# claude-toolkit

Personal Claude Code plugins, laid out as a private plugin marketplace. A proof of concept: it is compatible with the team-shared SDD skill but entirely separate from it, and never changes it. Every toolkit agent carries the `toolkit:` prefix.

## What it does

Open a project in VS Code and a **coordinator** Claude session starts in an editor tab. It reports the SDD team recap, reads the project board and asks what is next. You tell it the goal; it creates the **worker** sessions the job needs, each in its own named tab with a written brief, and follows them through SendMessage. Workers that still have open work reopen with their conversation the next time you open the project. You can still type in any worker's tab.

| Part | Where |
|---|---|
| `toolkit:coordinator` and `toolkit:worker` agents | `plugins/toolkit/agents/` |
| Start-up hook: runs SDD's team-mailbox pull for the coordinator only | `plugins/toolkit/hooks/` |
| VS Code extension: starts the coordinator, reopens active workers, opens requested workers | `vscode/` |

One project at a time; coordinating several projects is planned.

## Set up (once per machine)

Link the extension into VS Code, then reload VS Code (Command Palette → "Developer: Reload Window"):

```
New-Item -ItemType Junction -Path "$env:USERPROFILE\.vscode\extensions\dserri.claude-toolkit-0.0.1" -Target "<clone>\vscode"
```

The extension starts every session with `--plugin-dir <clone>/plugins/toolkit` and `--permission-mode auto` (sessions in the same mode exchange messages without approval prompts). `claude` must be on `PATH`, or set `claudeToolkit.claudePath`; `claudeToolkit.pluginDir` overrides the plugin folder.

## Enable a project

Open the project folder and run "Toolkit: Enable coordinator in this folder". It records the folder as enabled on this machine (in the extension's own storage, never in the repository), creates `.coord/`, adds it to `.git/info/exclude` (never `.gitignore`), and opens the coordinator. From then on the coordinator opens whenever VS Code opens the folder; "Toolkit: Start coordinator" opens it again if you closed it. A repository that carries a `.coord/` folder starts nothing until you enable it yourself, and the extension's settings are machine-scoped, so a workspace cannot change which executable or plugin it runs.

### The board (`.coord/`)

| File | Written by | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `team.json` | coordinator | `[{ "name", "role", "state": "active" \| "done" }]`; active workers reopen at start-up |
| `workers/<name>/brief.md` | coordinator | the worker's task |
| `workers/<name>/status.md` | worker | `State`, `Summary`, `Next` |
| `requests/<name>.json` | coordinator | `{ "name": "<name>" }`: asks the extension to open the worker; rejected requests leave `<name>.rejected.md` |
| `log.md` | coordinator | decisions, assignments and outcomes |
| `sessions/<session name>.id` | start-up hook | each worker's session ID, so its tab resumes exactly its own conversation, also when the coordinator requests a finished worker again |

Sessions are named `<project>-coordinator` and `<project>-<worker>` (the project folder name in lowercase, other characters as hyphens); tabs show the short name. Enabled projects need different folder names, or their sessions share names.

## Session status

The "Claude sessions" view (Explorer sidebar) and the status-bar item show every interactive Claude Code session on this machine, toolkit or not:

| Colour | Status | Set by |
|---|---|---|
| red | waiting for permission / waiting for your answer | `PermissionRequest`; `AskUserQuestion`, or a turn ending with `STATUS: QUESTION` (coordinator and worker) or a final `?` |
| purple | possibly stuck | working with no event for `claudeToolkit.stuckMinutes` (default 10) |
| yellow | finished, needs review | any other end of turn |
| green | working | a prompt or a tool result |
| grey | idle | session started, no prompt yet |

Cards are grouped by project folder (the most urgent project first; each group shows how many of its sessions wait) and sorted by urgency inside each group (longest waiting first) and show the time in that status, the last tool used ("after Bash"; only finished tool calls are recorded) or the tool asking for permission, and the last line of the last message. Click a card to focus its tab, in any VS Code window: each window lists the session tabs it opened in `~/.agent-status/windows/<pid>.json`, and a click on a session held by another window brings that window to the front (by opening its folder) and asks it, through `~/.agent-status/focus/<pid>.json`, to show the tab. A card's tooltip says where its session runs; a session started by hand outside the toolkit's tabs only gets a message. Hide a card with its eye icon until the session's next event. Closing a tab hides its card.

Install the hooks once (they back up `~/.claude/settings.json` first and add only their own entries):

```
node <clone>/status/install.mjs
node <clone>/status/install.mjs --uninstall
```

The hook (`status/status-hook.mjs`) runs asynchronously, so sessions never wait for it, and appends one line per event to `~/.agent-status/sessions/<session_id>.jsonl`; errors go to `~/.agent-status/hook.log`. It deletes a session's file at `SessionEnd` and leaves a `<session_id>.ended` marker so late background events cannot bring the session back (a new start or resume clears it), and, when a session starts, removes files and markers idle for more than 6 hours (`STALE_HOURS` at the top of the script). Headless sessions (`claude -p`, SDK, SDD's reviewer) are skipped by the observed but undocumented `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=sdk-*` value; `tests/status-entrypoint.e2e.mjs` checks it against the installed CLI. A denied permission stays red until the turn ends, because Claude Code fires no event for a denial.

## Plugin delivery

The organization's managed Claude Code policy currently allows only the official Anthropic marketplace, so the plugin is loaded from the clone with `--plugin-dir` (the extension does it; by hand: `claude --plugin-dir <clone>/plugins/toolkit`). Update with `git pull`, then reload VS Code.

Once an admin allows the marketplace:

```
claude plugin marketplace add dserri/claude-toolkit
claude plugin install toolkit@claude-toolkit
```

and enable auto-update for `claude-toolkit` in `/plugin` → Marketplaces. The plugin declares no version, so every pushed commit is a release.

## Roll back

Delete the `dserri.claude-toolkit-0.0.1` junction and reload VS Code; remove a project's `.coord/` folder if you no longer want its board. Sessions started by hand work as before.

## Develop

```
node --test
node --test tests/coordinator.e2e.mjs tests/status-entrypoint.e2e.mjs
```

The first runs the unit, hook, installer and `claude plugin validate` tests (`claude` must be on `PATH`). The second starts real headless sessions with a model call. Tab behaviour and the session view in VS Code are verified by hand.

# Design

## Context

See proposal.md. Verified on this machine: running `code <folder>` for a folder already open in a window brings that window to the front, and Windows allows it. Each window's extension already tracks the session names of the tabs it opened (`tabsBySession`). Session files hold only the folder name, not the path. The previous review left three advisory findings: a late async event after SessionEnd recreates the session file; the card itself does not say where a session runs; the archived proposal says "running tool".

## Goals / Non-Goals

**Goals:** one click reaches the right tab in any window; no server or background process.

**Non-Goals:** focusing sessions running outside the extension's tabs (hand-started terminals, other apps); the supervisor.

## Decisions

- **Window registry files** instead of session-level paths: `~/.agent-status/windows/<pid>.json` = `{ pid, folder, sessions: [names] }`, written on start and on every tab open/close, deleted on deactivate. A file whose pid no longer runs (`process.kill(pid, 0)` throws) is ignored and removed by the next window that reads it. This tells exactly which window holds a session, so a click never opens a window for a session that has none.
- **Raising the window:** `vscode.commands.executeCommand('vscode.openFolder', Uri.file(folder), { forceNewWindow: true })`; VS Code focuses the window that already has the folder open instead of opening another. If that check fails in acceptance, fall back to running the VS Code CLI with the folder, which was verified directly.
- **Showing the tab:** the clicking window writes `~/.agent-status/focus/<target pid>.json` = `{ session, at }`; each window watches only its own file, shows the tab whose session name matches one of its own tabs, and deletes the file. Nothing in the request reaches a command line or path except the target pid, which comes from the registry, not from the request.
- **Ended marker:** at SessionEnd the hook deletes the session file and writes `<session_id>.ended`; any later event finding that marker records nothing. The marker is removed by the existing stale cleanup (6 hours).
- **Project from the project root** (found in acceptance: coordinators working in `.coord/` were grouped under `.coord`): the hook records the folder name of `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`, which Claude Code sets for hooks and which does not follow the agent's `cd`, falling back to `cwd`.
- **Latest session per title** (found in acceptance: a window reload kills its tabs without SessionEnd, and the in-memory "closed tab" hiding is lost with the reload): toolkit session names are unique by design, so an older session with the same title is dead or superseded; the view keeps only the latest. Sessions without a title are named after their folder and are never merged.
- **Card location in the tooltip**, from the registry: "in this window", "in window <folder>", or "not in a toolkit tab".
- **Archived wording:** correct "running tool" to "last tool used" in the archived `add-session-status` proposal.

## Risks / Trade-offs

- [`vscode.openFolder` might open a second window instead of focusing] → verified in acceptance; CLI fallback ready.
- [Two windows with the same folder] → the registry names the pid, so the request reaches the right window; raising by folder may bring the other one forward, a rare case left as is.
- [Registry left behind by a crash] → pid liveness check.

# Proposal

## Why

The session view shows sessions from every VS Code window, but a click only focuses tabs of the window it is in. With several projects open in several windows, the developer sees a red card and still has to hunt for the window. Opening a folder that is already open brings its window to the front (verified on this machine), so a click can reach any window without a server.

## What Changes

- Each VS Code window publishes which session tabs it holds in `~/.agent-status/windows/<pid>.json`, and removes the file when it closes.
- Clicking a card of a session held by another window asks that window to show the tab (a request file it watches) and brings the window to the front by opening its folder.
- A card says where its session runs (this window, another window by folder, or not a toolkit tab) in its tooltip.
- Fixes from the previous review: a late event after SessionEnd no longer recreates an ended session's card; the archived proposal's "running tool" wording is corrected.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities

None.

### Modified Capabilities

- `session-status`: focusing reaches tabs in other VS Code windows, cards say where their session runs, and ended sessions stay ended.

## Impact

- `vscode/` (view, window registry, focus requests), `status/status-hook.mjs` (ended marker), tests, README.
- New files under `~/.agent-status/windows/` and `~/.agent-status/focus/`.

# Spec Delta

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Window registry

Each VS Code window running the extension SHALL publish `~/.agent-status/windows/<process id>.json` with its folder and the session names of the tabs it opened, update it whenever such a tab opens or closes, and delete it when the window closes. Entries of windows whose process no longer runs SHALL be ignored.

#### Scenario: Two windows

- **WHEN** one window holds `rehlko-portal-coordinator` and another holds `api-coordinator`
- **THEN** each window's file lists only its own sessions and folder

#### Scenario: Crashed window

- **WHEN** a window's file remains after its process has ended
- **THEN** no window treats its sessions as focusable there

### Requirement: Cross-window focus

Clicking a card whose session is held by another window SHALL bring that window to the front by opening its folder and SHALL ask it, through `~/.agent-status/focus/<process id>.json`, to show the tab; the receiving window SHALL show the tab and delete the request. Requests SHALL carry only a session name, which the receiver matches against its own tabs.

#### Scenario: Session in another window

- **WHEN** the developer clicks the red card of `api-tester`, held by the `api` window
- **THEN** the `api` window comes to the front with the `tester` tab shown

#### Scenario: Session not in any window

- **WHEN** the developer clicks the card of a session started by hand outside the extension's tabs
- **THEN** no window opens and a message says the session is not a toolkit tab

### Requirement: Card location

Each card's tooltip SHALL say where its session runs: in this window, in another window (by folder), or not in a toolkit tab.

#### Scenario: Tooltip

- **WHEN** the developer hovers the card of a session held by the `api` window
- **THEN** the tooltip names the `api` window

### Requirement: One card per session name, in its project

A card's project SHALL be the first project folder recorded for the session, taken from its project root (`CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`, else the working folder), so moving into a subfolder does not move the card. When several sessions carry the same session title, only the one with the latest event SHALL be shown; sessions without a title are never merged.

#### Scenario: Agent changes folder

- **WHEN** a coordinator started in `rehlko-portal` runs commands inside `.coord/`
- **THEN** its card stays in the `rehlko-portal` group

#### Scenario: Restarted coordinator

- **WHEN** an earlier `rehlko-portal-coordinator` session was killed by a window reload and a new one started
- **THEN** only the new session's card is shown

### Requirement: Ended sessions stay ended

After SessionEnd, later events of the same session SHALL NOT recreate its card; the ended marker SHALL be removed with the other stale files.

#### Scenario: Late event after the end

- **WHEN** a Stop of a session is recorded after its SessionEnd
- **THEN** no card for that session appears

# Tasks

## 1. Hook

- [x] 1.1 Write an `.ended` marker at SessionEnd and record nothing for a session that has one; remove markers with the stale cleanup; verify with hook tests

## 2. Window registry and focus

- [x] 2.1 Add pure helpers (registry entry, live-window filter, location label, focus target) to `vscode/status-core.js` with tests
- [x] 2.2 Publish and remove the window file, watch the window's own focus request, and route clicks to this window, another window or a message in `sessions-view.js`; verify VS Code loads it without errors
- [x] 2.3 Correct the archived proposal wording and document cross-window focus in README

## 3. Acceptance

- [x] 3.1 With the developer and two VS Code windows, click a card held by the other window and verify the window comes to the front with the right tab; click a hand-started session and verify only a message appears

# Proposal

## Why

With many Claude Code sessions open in parallel, the developer loses track of which ones wait for an answer or a permission. The coordinator flags them, but it infers state, so it is slow and sometimes wrong. Session state must come from deterministic hook events and be visible at a glance, with one click to the waiting tab.

## What Changes

- Add a status hook registered at user level for every interactive Claude Code session (headless `claude -p` and SDK sessions are skipped). It runs asynchronously, so sessions never wait for it, and records each relevant event in a per-session file under `~/.agent-status/sessions/`.
- Add an installer that backs up `~/.claude/settings.json` and adds or removes only the toolkit's hook entries.
- Extend the VS Code extension with a "Claude sessions" view and a status-bar count: one card per session with a colour-coded status, how long it has been in it, the last line of its last message and the last tool used, sorted by urgency; clicking a card focuses its tab when the tab belongs to this window; a card can be hidden until the session's next event.
- Add a closing `STATUS: QUESTION` / `STATUS: DONE` line to the coordinator and worker prompts only; other sessions use the `AskUserQuestion` event and a question-mark heuristic.
- No server, no listening port, no background process. The coordinator does not read the state yet.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities

- `session-status`: deterministic per-session status from hook events, its storage, and its view in VS Code.

### Modified Capabilities

- `project-coordinator`: the coordinator and worker prompts end each turn with a status line.

## Impact

- New `status/` folder (hook and installer), new view code in `vscode/`, tests extended.
- User-level `~/.claude/settings.json` gains asynchronous hook entries pointing at the clone (backed up first); `~/.agent-status/` holds the state.
- Relies on an observed, undocumented environment variable (`CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT`) to skip headless sessions; a test pins it.
- SDD is unchanged; its headless reviewer sessions are skipped by the hook.
